# About your cover

Silver Plus Hospital and Mid Extras is a combined hospital and extras policy from Wattle Health Fund. Your hospital cover is classified as Silver Plus. Your cover started on 1 July 2024. Extras limits reset on 1 January each calendar year, and all amounts are in Australian dollars.

This summary explains what your policy covers. Read it with the Private Health Information Statement for your policy and the fund rules, which set out the full terms of your cover.

# Hospital cover

Your Silver Plus hospital cover pays towards the cost of treatment as a private patient in a private or public hospital for the clinical categories included in your policy.

## Private hospital admission

Accommodation and theatre fees at agreement private hospitals are covered for included clinical categories, after your excess. Wattle Health Fund has agreements with most private hospitals in Australia. Check whether your hospital is an agreement hospital before you are admitted.

## Your excess

Excess: $500 per person per calendar year, payable once per admission and no more than once each year. You pay the excess to the hospital when you are admitted.

## Medical fees and the gap

For in-hospital medical services, Medicare pays 75% of the Medicare Benefits Schedule fee and we pay the remaining 25%. If your doctor charges more than the schedule fee and does not use our gap scheme, you may have out-of-pocket costs. Ask your doctor for an estimate of fees before you are admitted.

## Waiting periods for hospital cover

| Treatment | Waiting period |
| --- | --- |
| Emergency admissions after an accident | None |
| Hospital psychiatric services, rehabilitation and palliative care | 2 months |
| All other hospital treatment | 2 months |
| Pre-existing conditions | 12 months |
| Pregnancy and birth | 12 months (not included in this policy) |

Medicines in hospital

Prescription medicines supplied while you are admitted are covered when they are related to the treatment you were admitted for and are approved for use in hospital.

# Clinical categories

Every hospital policy in Australia is described using standard clinical categories. Silver Plus policies include all of the categories required for Silver cover and may include some additional categories. Your policy covers the following categories:

Back, neck and spine: Covered

Investigation and treatment of the back, neck and spinal column, including spinal fusion.

Cataracts: Covered

Surgery to remove a cataract and replace it with an artificial lens.

Heart and vascular system: Covered

Investigation and treatment of the heart, heart-related conditions and blood vessels.

Joint replacements: Covered

Surgery for joint replacements, including revisions, resurfacing and partial replacements.

Dental surgery: Covered

Surgery to the teeth and gums, such as surgery to remove wisdom teeth and dental implant surgery.

Hospital psychiatric services: Covered

Hospital treatment of mental health conditions, including drug and alcohol dependence.

Rehabilitation: Covered

Physical rehabilitation in hospital after an illness, injury or surgery.

What covered means

You are treated as a private patient in a private or public hospital, with benefits for accommodation, theatre fees and medical fees as described in this summary, after your excess and any waiting period.

## Before you go to hospital

- Check that your treatment falls under a covered clinical category
- Ask your hospital whether it has an agreement with Wattle Health Fund
- Ask your specialist and anaesthetist for a written estimate of their fees
- Make sure any waiting periods have been served

# Restricted and excluded categories

Some categories have restricted cover, and some are not covered by this policy.

Insulin pumps: Restricted

Provision and replacement of insulin pumps for the treatment of diabetes.

Pregnancy and birth: Not covered

Hospital treatment for investigation and treatment of conditions associated with pregnancy and childbirth.

Weight loss surgery: Not covered

Surgery designed to reduce a person's weight, such as gastric banding and sleeve gastrectomy.

## What restricted cover means

For a restricted category, you are covered as a private patient in a shared ward of a public hospital only. If you choose a private hospital, benefits will not cover the full cost of accommodation and you could have significant out-of-pocket costs.

## Categories that are not covered

No benefits are paid for hospital treatment in a category that is not covered, other than in the limited circumstances allowed by law. To be covered for pregnancy and birth you would need to upgrade to a Gold hospital policy, and a 12 month waiting period would apply to the upgraded benefits.

Planning a family?

Pregnancy and birth is included only in Gold hospital policies. Upgrade at least 12 months before the expected date of delivery so that the waiting period has been served.

## Changing your cover

You can move to a higher or lower hospital tier at any time. Waiting periods apply to any higher benefits, and time already served on your current policy counts for the benefits it includes.

# Extras cover: Mid Extras

Mid Extras pays benefits for services from recognised providers. Benefits are paid up to the limits shown, and are never more than the amount you were charged.

## General dental

General dental: $800 per person per calendar year, 2 month waiting period. A fixed benefit is paid for each item number.

| Item | Service | Benefit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 011 | Comprehensive oral examination | $45.00 |
| 012 | Periodic oral examination | $40.00 |
| 022 | Intraoral periapical radiograph | $30.00 |
| 114 | Removal of calculus | $70.00 |
| 121 | Topical fluoride | $20.00 |

## Major dental

Major dental: 60% of the charge, up to $1,000 per person per calendar year, 12 month waiting period. Major dental includes crowns, bridges, dentures, root canal treatment and the surgical removal of wisdom teeth.

Orthodontics

Orthodontic treatment, such as braces and aligners, is not included in Mid Extras.

### Getting the most from your dental cover

- Ask your dentist for the item numbers of any planned treatment and call us for a quote
- Claim on the spot so you only pay the gap at the dental practice
- Your general dental limit does not carry over to the next calendar year

# Extras cover: optical and therapies

## Optical

### Glasses and contact lenses

Optical: 100% back up to $250 per person per calendar year, 6 month waiting period. Benefits are paid for prescription lenses only, including prescription glasses and contact lenses.

## Therapies

### Physiotherapy, chiropractic and remedial massage

A fixed benefit is paid for each consultation or treatment. A 2 month waiting period applies to each of these services.

- Physiotherapy: initial consultation (item 500) $55, subsequent consultation (item 505) $45.
- Chiropractic: initial consultation (item 1500) $50, subsequent consultation (item 1505) $40.
- Remedial massage: initial treatment (item 105) $40, subsequent treatment (item 205) $35. Providers must be recognised by Wattle Health Fund.

Physiotherapy, chiropractic and remedial massage share a combined limit of $700 per person per calendar year.

Example

Your initial physiotherapy consultation costs $95 and the next one costs $80. We pay $55 and $45, and the $100 in benefits counts toward the therapies combined limit.

Recognised providers

We pay benefits only for services from providers who hold current registration or membership of a professional association that we recognise. Check before your appointment by calling 1300 975 707.

### Not included

- Group classes, such as clinical pilates, unless provided one-on-one
- Massage provided at a day spa or as part of a beauty treatment
- Sunglasses, and frames bought without prescription lenses

# Extras cover: psychology and ambulance

## Therapies

### Psychology

Psychology: 60% of the charge up to $80 per session, to $500 per person per calendar year. A 2 month waiting period applies. Sessions claimed under a Medicare Better Access plan cannot also be claimed here.

## Ambulance

### Emergency ambulance

Emergency ambulance: 100% of the charge, unlimited, no waiting period. Cover applies to emergency transport by a state ambulance service when you are taken to hospital for immediate treatment.

## Not included in Mid Extras

- Orthodontics
- Hearing aids
- Podiatry and foot orthotics
- Dietetics and exercise physiology
- Non-emergency patient transport

Medicare and extras

Extras benefits are not payable for a service that also receives a Medicare benefit. If Medicare pays part of a consultation, you cannot claim the rest of it from your extras cover.

## Using your extras cover

Extras benefits are paid per person, so each person on the policy has their own limits. Limits start again on 1 January, and any amount you do not use in a calendar year does not carry over.

Receipts for psychology must show that the service was provided by a registered psychologist, with the session date, its length and the fee charged.

# Waiting periods and important information

| Extras service | Waiting period |
| --- | --- |
| General dental | 2 months |
| Major dental | 12 months |
| Optical | 6 months |
| Physiotherapy, chiropractic and remedial massage | 2 months |
| Psychology | 2 months |
| Emergency ambulance | None |

Waiting periods apply when you first join and when you upgrade to a higher level of cover. Time served on an equivalent policy with another Australian fund counts towards your waiting periods.

## Lifetime Health Cover

If you did not hold hospital cover by 1 July following your 31st birthday, a loading of 2% for every year over age 30 may be added to your hospital premium. The loading is removed after 10 years of continuous hospital cover.

## Medicare levy surcharge

Holding an appropriate level of private hospital cover means you will not pay the Medicare levy surcharge. The surcharge applies to some people with incomes above a threshold who do not hold hospital cover.

## Australian Government Rebate

The rebate is income tested. It is applied as a reduction to your premium unless you choose to claim it in your tax return.

## General exclusions

- Treatment received outside Australia
- Services that are not clinically necessary, or that are cosmetic
- Treatment covered by compensation, damages or another insurer
- Services provided by a family member or business partner

# Making a claim

## Ways to claim

- At your provider: Claim on the spot with your member card where the provider has a HICAPS terminal. You pay only the gap.
- In the app: take a photo of your itemised receipt and submit it in the Wattle Health app.
- By post: send a claim form and your receipts to the address on page 12.

Quote your membership number [POLICY_1] when you call or write to us about a claim.

## Time limits

Extras claims must be lodged within 2 years of the date of service. Hospital claims are usually sent to us directly by the hospital.

## Receipts

You need an itemised receipt for every extras claim. The receipt must show the provider's name and provider number, the patient's name, the date of service, the item number and the fee charged.

## When benefits are not payable

Benefits cannot be paid for services claimed from Medicare or another insurer. We may ask for more information before we pay a claim, and benefits are paid only while premiums are paid up to date.

Payment of benefits

Benefits are paid by direct credit to your nominated bank account, usually within 2 business days.

### Claim checklist

- The patient's name as it appears on your membership
- The provider's name, provider number and practice address
- The date of service, item number and fee for each service
- Proof that the account has been paid, unless you claimed on the spot
